acceptance_gates: Inventory candidate model families, exact artifacts, licenses, weight access, tokenizer, adapters, and provenance before selecting a candidate.
Establish a baseline capability and resource profile for each lawful candidate under comparable conditions.
Run all nine Builder contracts against each candidate, including cross-role identity separation and all shared capabilities.
Select a compact candidate by measured capability and resource performance, not by parameter count or file size alone.
If reducing a model, preserve the exact source artifact, recipe, data provenance, and toolchain; distinguish quantization from lossy distillation or pruning.
Run the same held-out suite after reduction and report every retained, degraded, lost, and untested capability.
Have at least two independent evaluators review raw outputs and deterministic integrity/authority tests; obtain a third review for material disagreement.
Build the reconstruction seed with checksums, licenses, tokenizer/runtime dependencies, external-weight declarations, and explicit recovery steps.
Restore the seed on a clean compatible host without deleting or modifying the source known-good artifacts.
Do not call the candidate a portable minimum model until the capability suite and clean-host recovery drill pass.
known_unknowns: No candidate model has been benchmarked against the nine Builder contracts.
No compression, quantization, distillation, pruning, or fine-tuning has been performed.
No target hardware resource ceiling has been measured or adopted.

The analytical/verifier Builder roles are role assignments, not independent model artifacts; a separate evaluator artifact or human/deterministic review path must be selected before any model is independently scored.
No larger-model expansion blueprint has been registered; architecture, tokenizer, source weights, training data, recipe, toolchain, license, and compute dependencies remain to be identified.
